sourceConclusions: The old predicate searches all document cmdk items, accepts textContent.includes(full fixture name), and takes the first match. It does not establish one exact option value or ownership by the opened control.

LaunchTeamDialog sorts values by teamName but permits displayName labels and descriptions. Its actual custom renderOption includes label and description. Therefore another option can have allowed text containing the fixture name while retaining another value.

The finite another-team/description-containing-fixture counterexample in0df016a1 follows from the actual render path. It is source reasoning, not observed DOM or an executed reproduction of the macOS failure.

The seeded known description and later template description do not contain the full UUID name. No archived catalog establishes the actual org-team collision. The known counterexample does not prove historical applicability.

SchedulesView.handleCreate clears editingSchedule; its create-dialog teamName prop is undefined. The current org-team tab is not passed as that prop. LaunchTeamDialog initializes selectedTeamName empty; its only assignments are the option callback and an empty reset.

For a non-disabled item, Combobox forwards its closure-captured option.value directly to onValueChange, then closes and clears search. The launch-dialog callback stores that name. No fixture-to-org translation appears in the reviewed chain.

The saved-prompt hook receives effectiveTeamName and updates only the separate review object. It also requires open/enabled/current request and a nonempty saved prompt; the display requires the same team identity. The original result of that saved-request read is not retained.

The original button has aria-controls pointing to the PopoverContent container ID. That container holds a distinct cmdk listbox with its own ID. A future owner join must not assume the button controls the inner listbox node directly.
The Creation caller supplies no id to this team Combobox. A future test-only guard must resolve the intended dialog/control without pretending a dedicated current ID exists.

CdpClient.click first polls the expression, separately evaluates it for scroll/center, and sends one press/release. A valid element predicate alone does not make the later physical recipient or React commit atomic. There is no demonstrated global click-helper fix.
